steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets and set aside.

Combine cream cheese, margarine, white sugar, and brown sugar. Blend in egg and vanilla. Add dry ingredients and mix well. Fold in chocolate chips. Drop by rounded teaspoonfuls onto prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 18 minutes, or until edges are slightly browned.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream Cheese Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: The addition of cream cheese in this chocolate chip cookie recipe results in deliciously moist, cake-like cookies. Easy to make and irresistible!
raw_recipe.name: Cream Cheese Chocolate Chip Cookies

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets and set aside.

review.reviewBody: I used butter instead of margerine and I doubled the chips called for. Because I wanted a less cakey cooky, I used baking SODA instead of powder. I agree with another reviewer that the uncooked dough was really fantastic but when you cook it, it dosen't taste as good. Sounds bizarre but it's true. This makes a ton, way more than 12 servings, unless each person has four or five cookies. 375* for ten minutes was just right. This would be GREAT with white chocolate chips and craisins. NOTE: I did use fat free cream cheese but I think that was kind of like putting the cart before the horse, if you really think about it.

Made these with real butter instead of margarine. Also reduced sugar to 2/3 cup each. Added two teaspoons cinnamon. Used semi-sweet chocolate chips. Reduced oven temp to 325. Baked for about 10 minutes. 

These cookies are fine...nothing to write home about. You don't really get the cream cheese flavor, which is a bummer. The dough is pretty sticky, but bakes up just fine. The flavor of the cookie is nice. The dough is really good. These cookies are great if you have some cream cheese you need to use up, but I don't know that I'd go out of my way to make them again. Still...not bad.

I am highly satisfied with this recipe, I used it as a replacement for the chocolate walnut cream cheese pound cake my Aunt used to make! I used ghee in place of the margarine and lightly spread ghee on the cookie sheet in place of the butter spray and all wound up delicious!

I liked the overall flavor but I think with the extra cream cheese in an already properly portioned standars chocolate cookie recipe like this is, it reduces the sweetness. If you like less sweet items then its probably perfect but myself and others that tried this all thought it was bit too bland batterey. Next time Im going to increase the sugars to one full.cup.each instead of the 3/4. Also,again since the batter amount increased due to.8 oz cream cheese, the chocolate chips spread out a little too much so upping that as well to 2-1/2 cups

I used real butter, and white chocolate chips instead of semi-sweet and these cookies were FANTASTIC!! Only had to bake it my oven 13 minutes and I did flatten the dough somewhat but these cookies did spread on their own as well. Easy to make and delicious!!

These were okay - I made the dough and didn't have time to make cookies, so I baked it as a bar cookie in a jelly roll pan. Several people at work said they would have liked the bars more without chocolate chips in them. I think the basic dough is fine, I'm not sure chocolate chips are the best addition. I think I might use this dough and add toasted pecans, craisins and white chocolate chips (still make them as bar cookies, though). The basic dough is worth using in some way - just not perfectly suited to chocolate.
Addendum - I did make these again with the above noted additions and it was much better. I will make them again the new way.
I don't use margarine & I used butter & I used Lily's dark chocolate chips. So just tweak it to your own taste. I did!
Made with butter. THE BEST choc. chip cookies I've ever made and I've tried a lot .
These are delicious. Alterations: 2/3 c granulated sugar (vs 3/4c) 1 Table spoon vanilla (vs 1 tsp) 1 c semi-sweet chocolate chip and 1 c milk chocolate chip (vs 2 c same) About 12 minutes bake time

I put the first batch in for 16 minutes (recipe called for 15-17). Bottoms were burnt. Second batch I put in for 13 minutes. Bottoms were still too dark. I used the butter flavored spray for the first 2 batches and it burnt badly on the pan so for the third batch I used Crisco and reduced the heat to 350 and baked for 13 minutes. Bottoms were not as burnt but still not happy with them. Will never make this recipe again!

Thought they would melt flat due to the cream cheese - i was so surprised when my timer went off and the cookies poofed up not flattened.. i LOVE THESE not overly sweet love the cookie/cake cookie. Made them 3 times!!! NOT GOOD-LOL-I LIVE ALONE!! very addicting. going to make another batch tomorrow! I added some M&Ms ( ran short on chocolate chips) the more i cook the longer I have been leaving them in the oven started out at 10 min- now 15? :)

I followed the recipe but used mini semi-sweet chocolate chips since it’s all I had and the cookies taste great! I did change the oven temperature to 350 instead of 375 since the first batch burned on the bottom. I would make them again.

Flavor was not the banging chocolate chip cookie I expected. Especially adding cream cheese.. I wasnt expecting to have drop cookies either but if you're prepared to smash every one of them I guess it's an okay make. Very simple.
Maybe I did something wrong - but these cookies were extremely dry with little flavor.
The best chocolate chip cookies 🍪 EVER! I always use this recipe now. Great recipe if you don't have eggs.

i had been making these cookies for decades, then I became disabled and forgot the recipe I used. I tried this recipe and I must say my family loved them. I did vary it a bit by adding chopped walnuts instead of choc chips. Now they insist I make both kinds LOL
Excellent chocolate chip cookie! I used dark chocolate chips and added in walnuts!
